summary: I scanned m = 16..40 over all primes ≤ 3·10^6 (the PW Cor 2.2/2.4 scanner scripts/emn2_scan.c) and combined this with PW Table 1 for m = 8..15. For m ≥ 16 (uncensored, n = 19) the fit is log N_m ≈ 2.09·m^{0.505±0.14}, matching PW's exp(m^{1/2}) heuristic; ln N_m/√m ≈ 1.9–2.4 for odd m and 2.7–3.3 for 4 | m. The 4 | m excess is the known persistence of T1 for 4 | m (ident_numerators.md, POINTWISE_MN Lemma 1.1); a brute-force check of n = 9..169 confirms Type I/II are empty at odd squares exactly for m = 4, 8, 12, 16. 19/33 largest exceptions are ≡ 1 (mod m), and exceptions concentrate in square classes for all m. m = 4 (N_4 = 1) is consistent with the trend, which extrapolates to only e^{2–4}, so the calibration has no surprise. Caveat: m = 20, 28, 32, 36, 39, 40 are censored at 3·10^6, and a 10^9 run needs a sieve-based scanner.

The first step has a one-line answer already recorded in the repo: odd greedy never terminates within three terms for 4/n, n odd, because n(xy+yz+zx)=4xyz forces an even denominator (parity; greedy_algorithm_dynamics.md §1). The alt step (signature-0079, min offset k with 4/p−1/(⌈p/4⌉+k) a 2-term sum) is exactly J(p)=(a_min−3)/4 of Prop B.2 there, with its distribution to 3·10^5 (§4) and the window census to 10^8 (POINTWISE_SIZE §8). The existence-vs-algorithm caution is Theorem M/C (B1).

Checked whether the six U(n) sporadics {105, 2961, 3985, 25305, 111969, 978145} fit an RS-type 'sporadic set' pattern; FOREST_INVERSE.md §3.4 (CERTIFIED to 10^8/10^9) already settles it. All six are composites divisible by 3 or 5. U holds at every prime ≤ 10^9 and at every composite coprime to 105, and the sporadics are explained there as a 'loaded lottery': a prime q | n removes the coprime lines q | v, and the least QNR is enriched (r(n) ∈ {11,11,13,13,17,37}). This is not a finite-index sub-orbit phenomenon (U is not known to be an RS orbit: ES_APPROACH_GENERATORS §1), so the RS comparison adds nothing beyond z36_reciprocity_obstruction_home.md.

The first step (measure the dependency structure of ES events at fixed p and compare with Erdős–Tetali/Janson hypotheses) was already done in s9_janson_dependency.md (scripts/s9_janson.c, 108 283 primes ≤ 3·10^6). Word-level Δ/μ = 3.6→9.4 and μ²/2Δ = 0.85→1.82 ≪ log p. The near-independent units are levels, with expected count only (0.44→0.97)·log p, i.e. exactly critical for the >log n exponent that the Erdős–Tetali union bound needs. s9_lower_tail_literature.md already records the decisive difference: Erdős–Tetali chooses the random set, while ES's set is fixed. The alt step (Poisson c·log²p fit) is the FRONTIER §2.4 zero-law measurement.

Logic/literature check. Erdős–Fuchs needs a representation function of the form r_{A+A} (generating function f(z)² for a 0/1 series f). ES's R(n) has generating series Σ_{t,u,v} q^{tuv−u−v} (METAPLECTIC_ES Thm K), which is not of that form, so the theorem does not apply. The natural fluctuation statement for Σ_{n≤N} R(n) is a Hardy/Voronoi-type Ω-bound for divisor sums D_{4C}^−(4Cn+1) in progressions, which is a statement about averages with no pointwise content. Erdős–Turán's direction (coverage ⇒ unbounded multiplicity) is the converse of what ES needs and is already known for ES via Linnik (FRONTIER §2.2, Prop 3.1: R(p) ≥ exp(c log p/log log p) infinitely often).

The requested enumeration (natural finite ES-like sets S_p with windmill-type involutions, parity of |S_p| over p and over all n) is the content of WINDMILL.md §3 (~7000 weights on primes) and invol_windmill_signature.md §4. E1–E3 do GF(2) span tests of 288–385 natural weighted counts against divisor-type and 1564 binary-form parity vectors for n ≤ 2·10^4; E4 uses the always-odd set X(p) = {p = uvt−u−v}, PROVED odd for prime p ≥ 5, but its odd point (p+2,1,1) is not an ES certificate. The only divisor-type parity found is the trivial TI&x=y count, and the 'transpose-only' verdict quoted in the item is that memo's own result. No new set suggested itself within the time box that is not in the tested span.

I computed Δ_m(N) = max_a #{d|N : d ≡ a (mod m)} for N = 4Cp+1, m = 4C, C ∈ {1,2,3,5,6,10,15,30}, using 298 primes p ≡ 1 (24) near 10^7 and 300 composite controls n ≡ 1 (24). The maximising class is the trivial class 1 in 94–100% of cases, because d ≡ 1 and N/d ≡ 1 pair up and 1, N are always in it. Δ/τ and P(D^−>0) are indistinguishable between primes and controls (e.g. C=1: 0.729/0.557 vs 0.720/0.567). The max-class concentration function therefore carries no information about the ES class −1. The FKT random-divisor-walk methods address interval concentration, and the class analogue reduces to the already-studied one-class lottery D^−.

FUNCTIONFIELD_ES.md already gives the ingredient map that the item asks for. The fixed-q density-0 theorem (Thm 5.3) uses only the prime polynomial theorem in APs (Weil), which over ℤ is replaced by Bombieri–Vinogradov, so it is the analogue of Vaughan-type averages (§5 remark 3). The every-P theorems (Thm 6.1 for F_2 with A=T², ES_4(T) by finite covering, §6.2) rest on two PROVED mechanisms with no ℤ-analogue. (a) In char 2 and 3, 1 ≡ −1 resp. −2, so the size-obstructed class becomes trivially solvable. (b) T^q−T confines all primes to few classes (one class for q=2), and no modulus over ℤ does this. FUNCTIONFIELD_ES2/3 extend this to q=3,4. So the 'last ingredient' is a characteristic/degree degeneracy, not an RH-type input.
evidence: FUNCTIONFIELD_ES.md §§5–6 ('Why this exists over F₂ and not over Z')

summary: The requested factor/character pattern of the U(n) sporadics is already computed and certified in FOREST_INVERSE.md §3.4 (factorisations, n mod 24, least QNR r(n), nearest-square distance, 436 U_cop failures ≤ 10^8 all divisible by 3 or 5, none coprime to 105, U holds at all primes ≤ 10^9). So the U sporadic set is a composite small-prime-factor artefact, not a structured reciprocity family. The contrast with Ramanujan's 2719 holds only at the level of shape: Ono–Soundararajan's exceptions come from weight-3/2 L-values/GRH, while the U list is about lost lines at composite n. For ES itself the relevant sporadic set over primes is empty to 10^9.

I read Harpaz (arXiv:1511.04876v2, title verified; local PDF §1) and checked his hypotheses against U_n. His theorem covers pencils f(t,s)x² + g(t,s)y² = 1 whose generic fibre is a non-split norm-1 torus, and the proof runs 2-descent on that torus. Every conic fibration of the ES cubic, which is the 4-nodal Cayley cubic 1/x+1/y+1/z+1/W = 0 with W = −nw/4, has split fibres: fixing x gives ((4x−n)y−nx)((4x−n)z−nx) = n²x², and the pencil through the extra line {y=−x, z=n/4} gives residual conics with quadratic-part discriminant λ², a square (sympy, scripts/z52b_p1_H02_harpaz_conics.py). With split G_m-torsor fibres the Selmer machinery is vacuous: fibrewise integral points always exist, and ES's content sits entirely in the positivity and congruence conditions (the divisor lottery). So the hypotheses fail structurally, not only by S-integrality (cf. z31_integral_points_cubics §c).

The coverage-decay curve of identity families is the campaign's Haar avoider density δ*(T) of ET classes of modulus ≤ T. log(1/δ*) ≫ 𝓛³ is PROVED without log loss (CEILINGS_UNIFIED Prop 1.1), with upper bound ≪ 𝓛³(log𝓛)^5 (OMEGA13), and there are Monte Carlo/multilevel-splitting numerics (POINTWISE_HAAR §3: local exponent 2.26→2.58, Φ/(𝓛³/log𝓛) ≈ 0.07). That memo already compares this with sieve-dimension predictions. Reparametrising by number of families instead of modulus adds nothing; the non-coverage itself is the classical square-class obstruction (covering_distortion_dual.md §3 c1).

I computed the least covering modulus q = 4uB of the (★) system for every n ≡ 1 (4), n ≤ 4·10^6, and the uncovered non-squares as M = 2^k grows. Primes: 70 695 → 88 at M = 65 536 → 12 at M ≥ 4·10^6; the 12 are exactly the (★) census zeros. Composites: 3 265 remain, all of the small-factor 'lost lines' type. The uncovered-prime fraction decays like exp(−≈0.05(log M)²), slower than the Poisson rate e^{−M_BM} and consistent with the measured fat zero law (FRONTIER §2.4). Because the modulus at level C is ≈ n/C, the M-curve is the distribution of the largest certificate level, not a Haar covering density; the distortion/BBMST transfer is already dismissed in covering_distortion_dual.md (§3 c1–c4: B1/B6).

The repo has already exploited algebraic factorisations for thin families. Sophie Germain 4X⁴+1 closes 3·2^s+1 (z15_proth_sophie_germain, DISCOVERIES 74), cyclotomic/Aurifeuillean factors of 4^r+1 close 4^s+105 (s6_exp_classes_105), and a cyclotomic moving-gap class closes 63·2^s+1 (DISCOVERIES 80). Quadratic families p = m²+k with Aurifeuillean splitting of (m²+k)²+4c²d are classified as non-escaping (y10_poly_families_above / NEAR_SQUARE Thm 2.2), and Gaussian/Aurifeuille constructions from p = x²+y² collapse (z26_gaussian_aurifeuille). Bases 3, 5, 6, 7 were not enumerated, but that would only add thin exponential families, which by (J)76 do not transfer to primes. The only open use is the listed open families (15·2^s+1, 4^s+297).

For 5 primes p ≡ 1 (24) near 10^7 and C ≤ 3000 I measured the fraction of levels with no divisor ≡ −1 (mod 4C) of 4Cp+1. It is 0.6–0.8 for C ≤ 10, ≈0.95 for C ≤ 100 and ≈1.000 beyond 1000 (2–6 hits per decade). The semi-linear ('all odd prime factors ≡ 1 mod 4') set has frequency ≈0.25–0.28 and is only a subset of the failing levels. The inclusion runs the wrong way: Landau-type ⊂ fail(C), so an upper-bound half-dimensional sieve over C bounds a sub-event and says nothing about failure. Failure at a level is the typical outcome, because the modulus 4C moves with the level (the 'modulus is part of the solution' phenomenon). Summing over C reduces to the known critical level count (≈ log p expected hit levels, FRONTIER §2.4).

Heath-Brown's mechanism (Artin survey, Moree §'Heath-Brown'): Fouvry–Iwaniec/Chen sieve primes p with (p−1)/2 having ≤ 2 large prime factors. At such p, (ℤ/p)^× has only subgroups of large prime index, and a counting argument (few p with 2, 3, 5 all in one index-q subgroup) leaves at most 2 of 3 bases failing, for infinitely many p. The proposed ES analogue ('of three fixed (u,B) lines, at most two fail on a positive proportion of p') is trivially false: line (u,B) fires only on the class −(u+B) mod 4uB, so by CRT all three fail on density ∏(1−1/φ(4u_iB_i)) > 0 (the B1 statement). The H-B structure has no counterpart, since ES's groups (ℤ/4C)^× are small and have no large-prime-index subgroups, and 'infinitely many p' is trivial for ES (residue classes). This is the F34 'infinitely often' regime, not every-p.

The target-Davenport question is answered in z33_target_davenport.md (PROVED). The target constant η(G) is infinite without a subgroup condition, because sequences inside H ∌ −1 never hit −1 (the T1 shadow). With escapers, an element of order 2n gives η ≥ n−1, and for t = 4q (q ≡ 3 mod 4 prime) η ≥ (q−3)/2. Each N supplies ≤ 1 forced escaping large factor per subgroup, and large primes are private to one N, so zero-sum forcing works only where η = 0, i.e. exponent-2 levels t | 24. polynomial_method.md (b3) adds that Chevalley–Warning/Davenport certify the identity, not −1. The 'Ω vs D' comparison is subsumed (Erdős–Kac Ω ≈ log log p ≪ D((ℤ/4C)^×) except at tiny C).

The projective ES surface is the 4-nodal Cayley cubic (cayley_markoff_cm P1). Its 9 lines and universal torsor X_i = ε y_j y_k y_l z_ij z_ik z_il are classical (Heath-Brown 2003, Lemma 1, N(B) ≍ B(log B)^6), and ET Remark 2.10 identifies Type I/II as torsor coordinates; graph_cayley_moves.md §2 records both, checked in LITERATURE_2026. So the comparison of ET variables with Cox-ring generators is done. Integral points on the torsor are the ET parametrisation itself, i.e. the divisor lottery (B2). Nothing new remains in the item.
evidence: Heath-Brown, The density of rational points on Cayley's cubic surface (2003)

summary: The exact Chebotarev/CRT densities of primes solved by ET families of modulus ≤ M are the Haar avoider density δ*(T), already bounded and computed: log 1/δ* ≍ 𝓛³ up to (log𝓛)^5 (CEILINGS_UNIFIED Prop 1.1, OMEGA13 Thm 3.4), with Monte Carlo values in POINTWISE_HAAR §3 and conjectured exponent a = 3. The 'Rédei/Markov-chain model vs data' alternative is the level-independence study (s9_janson_dependency: per-level events near-independent). Stevenhagen's Markov chain is specific to 2-Selmer ranks with a group-structured state space; ES certificate classes have no such rank-type state, and nothing in the item supplies one.

Read literally (constant numerator 4 ∈ F_q), the char-3 question is trivial in every characteristic: 1/P = 1/(P+2) + 1/((P+1)(P+2)) + 1/(P(P+1)) (monic, degrees n, 2n, 2n; checked by hand). In char 2, 4/P = 0 does not depend on P at all, so neither case separates anything. The repo's analogue (FUNCTIONFIELD_ES §1) correctly replaces 4 by a monic A of degree k ≥ 1. There the numerator's role in char 2/3 is already isolated: Prop 1.4(iii) shows ES_q(T,P) holds for all P over F_2, F_3, and §6.1(a) shows the class-1 size obstruction collapses because 1 ≡ −1, −2. bsE_large_q_char3.md treats char 3 at large q.

Bir(Cayley cubic) ≅ Cremona group via X_i ↦ 1/X_i, acting transitively off a thin set, so its 'connectivity' is content-free (graph_cayley_moves.md M3). The integral affine symmetry group of the ES equation has order 4 (WINDMILL Prop 2), U_n has no Vieta involutions (cayley_markoff_cm P3), and its automorphism group is finite (thin_group_orbits §3). The one natural cross-n move (chord–tangent) provably never sends two positive solutions to a positive one (graph_cayley_moves Thm A.1/Cor A.2; experiment over 65 703 chords). A BGS-type Vieta action on U_n therefore does not exist in any computed form; the mod-ℓ graph of the item would be built from moves already shown to be finite or positivity-breaking.

Ramsey-ES is false, by an elementary scale argument (PROVED). For prime p every solution has min denominator ≤ 3p/4 and max ≥ p^{3/2}/2: Type I forces x ≥ p(p+1)/4, and Type II needs p | 4y'z'−y'−z', so y'z' ≥ p/4. Also max ≤ 1.2p^4. The 2-colouring c(n) = ⌊log_8 log_2 n⌋ mod 2 therefore has no monochromatic solution for every prime p with log_2 p ∈ [(2/3)·8^{j+1}+2, 8^{j+1}), i.e. infinitely many p (min z/p = 11 for p ∈ [300,3000] agrees). Residue colourings reduce to numerator problems: mono mod 3 ⇔ 12/p and mono mod 4 ⇔ 16/p are 3-term representable (other classes are killed by congruence/parity), so they fail at Schinzel exceptions. Brute force over p ≤ 3000 (13 colourings) shows many failures. Croot-type density arguments cannot reach ES through this strengthening.

Large sieve with C-form classes as the sifting classes: the exceptional-set large-sieve programme is fully worked out in EXCEPTIONAL_LARGESIEVE.md–LARGESIEVE7.md. Exact duality (Thm 2.1) makes every CRT-admissible large sieve a Selberg-square majorant, and Thm 3.1 caps its saving at (log N)^{3/4}; this covers Montgomery, Montgomery–Vaughan, weighted, multiplicative, composite-moduli and fibrewise forms. Gallagher's larger sieve is capped by a χ² functional (Thm 6.2), and the only remaining escape is H_LS (LARGESIEVE2). The item's X/log²X bound is far weaker than Vaughan's exp(−c(log N)^{2/3}) and the campaign's 3/4 note, and its ω(a) ≈ τ((a+1)/4) form is one of the forced-class mixtures covered by Thm 3.1.

Pseudosquare-type stress tests are already in the repo. DISPROOF_AVENUES §5 ran adversarial designs at 10^18–10^25: D1, p ≡ 1 mod the primorial up to 37/43/53 (stronger than pseudosquare at those primes), and D2 = D1 plus (ℓ/p) = +1 for all ℓ ≤ 97, the explicit pseudosquare proxy. The depression saturates at 0.26–0.36 × controls in the cheap families (realistic total ≈ 0.7–0.8), and no prime came near failure (min 612 solutions). z52b fingerprint items 13/14/22 computed U(p)/log²p at least-QNR record primes ≤ 8·10^6 (0.29–0.67, moderately low, not record-hard; 2521 is harder at 0.15) and found residual correlation ρ = −0.66 with least QNR. Running actual Lehmer pseudosquares from A002189 would add points of the same kind; it is a well-defined but low-value extension.

I computed R(p) (the (★) count) for all 69 108 primes p ≡ 1 (4) in [10^6, 3·10^6] and the Gaussian angle θ_p (p = a²+b², a odd). I regressed log(R+1) on log p and p mod 48 class indicators and correlated the residual with the Hecke characters cos(4kθ_p), k = 1, 2, 3. All correlations are null: Spearman −0.003, −0.005, −0.001 (p = 0.45, 0.21, 0.71; SE ≈ 0.004), and mean residuals per θ-octile are within ±0.006 against residual sd 0.317. The Gaussian angle carries no ES-hardness information beyond congruences at this scale, as expected; this rules out a ℤ[i]-angle route.

Not actionable as stated. Conductor bounds need an additively closed set (a numerical semigroup), and no ES certificate set has that. The word sets {tuv−u−v} are not closed under addition, and the only additive moves (d ↦ d+1 in ET coordinates, n ↦ n+4ab) generate residue classes, i.e. B1 congruence families, not semigroups. 'Largest missing admissible divisor residue mod 4C' is undefined for a fixed modulus, since the target class −1 is fixed and the divisor set is per-integer. The one honest Frobenius echo is already in the repo: t = 1 words uv−u−v are Sylvester's Frobenius numbers g(u,v), and the co-finiteness statement I3 ('every n > 2 433 600 is tuv−u−v with t,u,v ≥ 3', CERTIFIED to 10^9) is the conductor-type statement. A web search found no Frobenius/ES literature link.
evidence: web search 'Erdős-Straus conjecture Frobenius number numerical semigroup' (no hit)
